issues.issue: "Terminal Illness" turns on an illness "expected to result in the insured's death within six months based on evidence satisfactory to us", combining a prognosis standard with the insurer's own satisfaction. Who decides, and on what basis, is left to the insurer.

"Our discounting rate will be subject to the higher of: 1. 5%; or 2. the Published Monthly Average" does not say whether that higher figure is a ceiling or a floor on the rate used to discount the benefit. The direction of the constraint determines whether the insured is paid more or less.

The sentence is broken ("The discounted del any other 5 then current Administrative Charge"), so what is deducted from the discounted benefit besides the Administrative Charge cannot be read. The deduction that fixes the payment is incompletely stated.

The enumerated list is garbled (items run together with the stray characters "Oo PWN"), and it directs that "any policy debt including any unpaid loan interest" be "reduced by the Proportion" alongside the face amount and cash value. Whether the debt reduction is a benefit to the owner or a drafting slip is not resolvable from the text.

The paragraph presupposes a variable policy with Separate Account subaccounts, whereas this contract is a fixed-interest universal life policy whose Section 9 credits a declared interest rate. The provision has no subject matter in this instrument.

The statement that "[t]he policyowner will be responsible to pay the premiums ... in order to keep the policy in force" does not fit a flexible-premium policy, where Section 10 permits but never requires premium payments and Section 11 makes lapse turn on Policy Value. The rider imports a fixed-premium obligation the policy does not create.

The bar covers claims of "any creditor, trustee in bankruptcy or governmental agency, or arising under any court order directed against you", a general phrase appended to a specific list whose reach — for instance to a family-court or tax order — is unsettled. The qualifier "to the extent that we have written notice thereof" adds a further indeterminate limit.

The declaration is a compound negative — "no insured has applied to any insurance company or society without receiving the exact policy applied for or had any symptoms, diseases or disorders for which advice has been sought" — in which the "without" governs the first limb but not obviously the second. What exactly is being represented is uncertain, and rescission may turn on it.

The statement that "Home Office approval of form #519B is necessary before the policy is in effect" adds a condition of effectiveness not found in Section 10 of the policy or in the application's own list of conditions for insurance to take effect. The conditions precedent are stated in three places in different terms.

"Premiums are payable as shown on the schedule page of this policy" reads as a fixed obligation, whereas the policy is a flexible-premium contract in which the Schedule's Planned Premium is only an intention and Section 10 imposes no duty to pay. The two characterisations of the premium obligation differ.

The first-year figure of $299,526 does not match the application's Section V entries for first-year anticipated and subsequent planned premium. The amendment and the incorporated application state different premium figures.

The beneficiary section is reproduced with the sentences interleaved and the handwritten entries partly illegible, so the identity of the designated primary beneficiary and the share percentages cannot be read from the form itself. The default sharing rule is broken across the fragments.

The Total Face Amount applied for is illegible on the face of the form ("$_2)_ Jo, WD"), so the amount of coverage requested cannot be determined from this section. It is the operative figure of the coverage request.

The face amount recorded here does not correspond to the $6,000,000 stated in the Policy Acceptance Form amendment and the Schedule Pages. The application, which is made part of the policy, and the Schedule state the coverage differently.

The premium figures entered here ("103,397" and "453597") and the checked "Option 4 Level Face Amount" do not match the Schedule Pages' Planned Premium of $299,526 and "Death Benefit Option A". Since Section 22 makes the application part of the entire contract, the two documents state the terms differently.

The election refers to allocating premiums "to the Money Market subaccount until the end of the Right to Cancel Period, as stated in the policy", but this policy has no subaccounts and its front page provides a Right to Return with a full premium refund. The option described does not exist under the instrument.

The five conditions for the insurance to take effect — including that all representations "remain true, complete and accurate" and that there be no change in health — differ from Section 10 of the policy, which conditions coverage only on underwriting approval, satisfaction of the application conditions and receipt of the Minimum Initial Premium. They also sit against the Incontestability provision.
